questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A person observes several trees in an open space, with the following details given. Arrange the trees in decreasing order of their apparent sizes.
TreeHeight (m)Distance from the eye (m)
A$2.0$$50$
B$2.5$$80$
C$1.8$$70$
D$2.8$$100$
questions.solution:
The apparent size of an object is proportional to the visual angle it subtends at the eye. For small angles, this angle is given by $\theta \approx \dfrac{h}{d}$, where $h$ is the height of the object and $d$ is its distance from the eye.

Calculating the visual angle for each tree:

For tree A: $\theta_A = \dfrac{2.0}{50} = 0.040$ rad

For tree B: $\theta_B = \dfrac{2.5}{80} = 0.03125$ rad

For tree C: $\theta_C = \dfrac{1.8}{70} \approx 0.0257$ rad

For tree D: $\theta_D = \dfrac{2.8}{100} = 0.028$ rad

Comparing the angles, we get $\theta_A > \theta_B > \theta_D > \theta_C$.

The decreasing order of their apparent sizes is A, B, D, C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the image is formed at the near point ($25 \text{ cm}$) of a normal eye, a simple microscope exhibits a magnifying power of $3.0$. Calculate the magnifying power of this microscope if the image is formed at infinity.
questions.solution:
The magnifying power of a simple microscope when the image is formed at the near point $D$ is given by $m = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$.

Given $m = 3.0$ and $D = 25 \text{ cm}$, we have:

$3.0 = 1 + \dfrac{25}{f}$

$\dfrac{25}{f} = 2.0$

The magnifying power when the image is formed at infinity is given by $m_{\infty} = \dfrac{D}{f}$.

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{25}{f}$, we get:

$m_{\infty} = 2.0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A child has a near point at $10 \text{ cm}$. Determine the maximum angular magnification the child can obtain using a convex lens of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
The maximum angular magnification of a simple microscope is obtained when the final image is formed at the near point of the eye.

The formula for maximum angular magnification is given by:

$m = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$

where $D$ is the near point distance and $f$ is the focal length of the convex lens.

Given:

$D = 10 \text{ cm}$

$f = 10 \text{ cm}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$m = 1 + \dfrac{10}{10}$

$m = 1 + 1 = 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the image is formed at the near point ($25 \text{ cm}$) of a normal eye, a simple microscope exhibits a magnifying power of $3.0$. Determine the focal length of the microscope.
questions.solution:
The magnifying power of a simple microscope when the image is formed at the near point is given by the formula:

$m = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$

where $m$ is the magnifying power, $D$ is the least distance of distinct vision (near point), and $f$ is the focal length of the lens.

Given:
$m = 3.0$
$D = 25 \text{ cm}$

Substituting the given values into the formula:

$3.0 = 1 + \dfrac{25}{f}$

$2.0 = \dfrac{25}{f}$

$f = \dfrac{25}{2.0} = 12.5 \text{ cm}$

The focal length of the microscope is $12.5 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is viewed using a simple microscope of focal length $12 \text{ cm}$. To obtain the maximum angular magnification, at what distance from the lens should the object be positioned? The least distance for clear vision is $25 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
For maximum angular magnification, the final image must be formed at the least distance of distinct vision.

Given:
Focal length, $f = +12 \text{ cm}$
Image distance, $v = -D = -25 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-25} - \dfrac{1}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{-12 - 25}{300} = -\dfrac{37}{300}$

$u = -\dfrac{300}{37} \text{ cm} \approx -8.1 \text{ cm}$

The object should be positioned at a distance of $8.1 \text{ cm}$ from the lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A simple microscope is rated at $5 \text{ X}$ for a normal relaxed eye. Determine its magnifying power for a relaxed farsighted eye that has a near point of $40 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
The magnifying power of a simple microscope for a relaxed eye (image at infinity) is given by $M = \dfrac{D}{f}$, where $D$ is the near point of the observer's eye and $f$ is the focal length of the lens.

For a normal eye, the near point is $D = 25 \text{ cm}$. Given that the magnifying power is $5 \text{ X}$, we have:

$5 = \dfrac{25}{f} \Rightarrow f = 5 \text{ cm}$

For a farsighted eye with a near point $D' = 40 \text{ cm}$, the magnifying power for a relaxed eye will be:

$M' = \dfrac{D'}{f} = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8$

Thus, the magnifying power is $8 \text{ X}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Determine the maximum magnifying power of a compound microscope equipped with a $25$ diopter lens as the objective and a $5$ diopter lens as the eyepiece, given a separation of $30 \text{ cm}$ between the two lenses. The least distance for clear vision is $25 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
Focal length of objective lens, $f_o = \dfrac{100}{P_o} = \dfrac{100}{25} = 4 \text{ cm}$

Focal length of eyepiece lens, $f_e = \dfrac{100}{P_e} = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20 \text{ cm}$

For maximum magnifying power, the final image is formed at the least distance of clear vision, $v_e = -25 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula for the eyepiece:

$\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$

$\dfrac{1}{-25} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_e} = -\dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{9}{100} \Rightarrow |u_e| = \dfrac{100}{9} \text{ cm}$

The separation between the lenses is $L = v_o + |u_e| = 30 \text{ cm}$.

$v_o = 30 - \dfrac{100}{9} = \dfrac{170}{9} \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula for the objective:

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$

$\dfrac{9}{170} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{9}{170} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{18 - 85}{340} = -\dfrac{67}{340} \Rightarrow |u_o| = \dfrac{340}{67} \text{ cm}$

The magnifying power of the objective is:

$m_o = \dfrac{v_o}{|u_o|} = \dfrac{170/9}{340/67} = \dfrac{67}{18}$

The magnifying power of the eyepiece is:

$m_e = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f_e} = 1 + \dfrac{25}{20} = \dfrac{9}{4}$

The maximum magnifying power of the compound microscope is:

$M = m_o \times m_e = \dfrac{67}{18} \times \dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{67}{8} = 8.375 \approx 8.4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a compound microscope, the separation between the objective and the eyepiece is adjustable between $9.8 \text{ cm}$ and $11.8 \text{ cm}$. Given that the focal lengths of the objective and the eyepiece are $1.0 \text{ cm}$ and $6 \text{ cm}$ respectively, determine the range of its magnifying power, provided the final image is always required at a distance of $24 \text{ cm}$ from the eye.
questions.solution:
For the eyepiece, using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$ with $v_e = -24 \text{ cm}$ and $f_e = 6 \text{ cm}$:

$\dfrac{1}{-24} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_e} = -\dfrac{1}{24} - \dfrac{1}{6} = -\dfrac{5}{24}$

$u_e = -4.8 \text{ cm}$

The magnification produced by the eyepiece is $m_e = \dfrac{v_e}{u_e} = \dfrac{-24}{-4.8} = 5$.

The distance between the objective and the eyepiece is $L = v_o + |u_e| = v_o + 4.8$.

For the minimum separation $L = 9.8 \text{ cm}$:

$v_o = 9.8 - 4.8 = 5.0 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula for the objective, $\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$:

$\dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{5} - 1 = -\dfrac{4}{5} \Rightarrow u_o = -1.25 \text{ cm}$

The magnification of the objective is $m_o = \dfrac{v_o}{u_o} = \dfrac{5}{-1.25} = -4$.

The magnifying power is $|M| = |m_o \times m_e| = |-4 \times 5| = 20$.

For the maximum separation $L = 11.8 \text{ cm}$:

$v_o = 11.8 - 4.8 = 7.0 \text{ cm}$

$\dfrac{1}{7} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{7} - 1 = -\dfrac{6}{7} \Rightarrow u_o = -\dfrac{7}{6} \text{ cm}$

The magnification of the objective is $m_o = \dfrac{v_o}{u_o} = \dfrac{7}{-\dfrac{7}{6}} = -6$.

The magnifying power is $|M| = |m_o \times m_e| = |-6 \times 5| = 30$.

Therefore, the range of its magnifying power is $20$ to $30$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An eye is capable of distinguishing between two points on an object if their separation is greater than $0.22 \text{ mm}$ when the object is held $25 \text{ cm}$ from the eye. This object is subsequently viewed through a compound microscope that has a $20 \text{ D}$ objective and a $10 \text{ D}$ eyepiece, separated by a distance of $20 \text{ cm}$. The final image is produced at $25 \text{ cm}$ from the eye. Determine the minimum separation between two points of the object that can now be distinguished.
questions.solution:
The focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece are given by:

$f_o = \dfrac{100}{P_o} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5 \text{ cm}$

$f_e = \dfrac{100}{P_e} = \dfrac{100}{10} = 10 \text{ cm}$

For the eyepiece, the final image is formed at the near point, so $v_e = -25 \text{ cm}$. Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$

$\dfrac{1}{-25} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_e} = -\dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{10} = -\dfrac{7}{50} \implies u_e = -\dfrac{50}{7} \text{ cm}$

The distance between the objective and the eyepiece is $L = 20 \text{ cm}$. The image distance for the objective is:

$v_o = L - |u_e| = 20 - \dfrac{50}{7} = \dfrac{90}{7} \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula for the objective:

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$

$\dfrac{7}{90} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{7}{90} - \dfrac{18}{90} = -\dfrac{11}{90} \implies u_o = -\dfrac{90}{11} \text{ cm}$

The linear magnification of the objective is:

$m_o = \left| \dfrac{v_o}{u_o} \right| = \dfrac{90/7}{90/11} = \dfrac{11}{7}$

The angular magnification of the eyepiece is:

$m_e = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f_e} = 1 + \dfrac{25}{10} = \dfrac{7}{2}$

The total magnifying power of the compound microscope is:

$M = m_o \times m_e = \dfrac{11}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{2} = 5.5$

The unaided eye can distinguish a minimum separation of $d = 0.22 \text{ mm}$ at a distance of $25 \text{ cm}$. When viewed through the microscope, the minimum separation $d_{min}$ on the object that can be distinguished is reduced by the magnification factor:

$d_{min} = \dfrac{d}{M} = \dfrac{0.22 \text{ mm}}{5.5} = 0.04 \text{ mm}$

Answer: $0.04 \text{ mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A compound microscope is composed of an objective with a focal length of $1 \text{ cm}$ and an eyepiece with a focal length of $5 \text{ cm}$. An object is positioned $0.5 \text{ cm}$ from the objective. Determine the separation between the lenses required for the microscope to project an inverted real image of the object onto a screen located $30 \text{ cm}$ behind the eyepiece.
questions.solution:
Using the lens formula for the objective lens:

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$

Substituting $u_o = -0.5 \text{ cm}$ and $f_o = 1 \text{ cm}$:

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{-0.5} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} + 2 = 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_o} = -1 \Rightarrow v_o = -1 \text{ cm}$

The image formed by the objective is virtual and is located $1 \text{ cm}$ in front of the objective.

For the eyepiece, the final image is real and is formed on a screen $30 \text{ cm}$ behind it. Using the lens formula for the eyepiece:

$\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$

Substituting $v_e = 30 \text{ cm}$ and $f_e = 5 \text{ cm}$:

$\dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{1 - 6}{30} = -\dfrac{5}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{6}$

$u_e = -6 \text{ cm}$

The intermediate image acts as the object for the eyepiece and is located $6 \text{ cm}$ in front of it.

Let the separation between the lenses be $L$. Since the intermediate image is $1 \text{ cm}$ in front of the objective, its total distance from the eyepiece is $L + 1 \text{ cm}$.

Therefore, $L + 1 = 6 \Rightarrow L = 5 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the image is formed at infinity, a compound microscope has a magnifying power of $100$. The focal length of the objective is $0.5 \text{ cm}$ and the tube length is $6.5 \text{ cm}$. Calculate the focal length of the eyepiece.
questions.solution:
For a compound microscope with the final image formed at infinity, the magnifying power is given by:

$M = |m_o| \times m_e = \left(\dfrac{v_o}{|u_o|}\right) \left(\dfrac{D}{f_e}\right)$

Using the lens formula for the objective lens, $\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$:

$\dfrac{v_o}{|u_o|} = \dfrac{v_o}{f_o} - 1$

The tube length $L$ of the microscope when the final image is at infinity is the distance between the objective and the eyepiece, which is given by:

$L = v_o + f_e \Rightarrow v_o = L - f_e$

Substituting $v_o$ into the magnification formula:

$M = \left( \dfrac{L - f_e}{f_o} - 1 \right) \left( \dfrac{D}{f_e} \right)$

Given values are:
$M = 100$
$f_o = 0.5 \text{ cm}$
$L = 6.5 \text{ cm}$
$D = 25 \text{ cm}$ (standard least distance of distinct vision)

Substituting the given values:

$100 = \left( \dfrac{6.5 - f_e}{0.5} - 1 \right) \left( \dfrac{25}{f_e} \right)$

$100 = \left( \dfrac{6.5 - f_e - 0.5}{0.5} \right) \left( \dfrac{25}{f_e} \right)$

$100 = \left( \dfrac{6.0 - f_e}{0.5} \right) \left( \dfrac{25}{f_e} \right)$

$100 = (6.0 - f_e) \times \dfrac{50}{f_e}$

$2 f_e = 6.0 - f_e$

$3 f_e = 6.0$

$f_e = 2 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An optical instrument employed for angular magnification contains an objective of $25 \text{ D}$ and an eyepiece of $20 \text{ D}$. When the eye is least strained, the tube length is $25 \text{ cm}$. What type of instrument is this?
questions.solution:
The focal length of the objective lens is $f_o = \dfrac{100}{P_o} = \dfrac{100}{25} = 4 \text{ cm}$.

The focal length of the eyepiece is $f_e = \dfrac{100}{P_e} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5 \text{ cm}$.

Since both the objective and the eyepiece have small focal lengths, the instrument is a compound microscope. In a telescope, the objective lens has a much larger focal length compared to the eyepiece.

For a telescope in normal adjustment (least strained eye), the tube length would be $L = f_o + f_e = 4 + 5 = 9 \text{ cm}$, which contradicts the given tube length of $25 \text{ cm}$.

For a microscope in normal adjustment, the tube length is $L = v_o + f_e$.

$25 = v_o + 5 \Rightarrow v_o = 20 \text{ cm}$.

Since $v_o > f_o$, the objective forms a real image, which is consistent with the principle of a compound microscope.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An optical instrument employed for angular magnification contains an objective of $25 \text{ D}$ and an eyepiece of $20 \text{ D}$. When the eye is least strained, the tube length is $25 \text{ cm}$. What is the angular magnification produced?
questions.solution:
Given the power of the objective lens, $P_o = 25 \text{ D}$, its focal length is:

$f_o = \dfrac{100}{P_o} = \dfrac{100}{25} = 4 \text{ cm}$

Given the power of the eyepiece, $P_e = 20 \text{ D}$, its focal length is:

$f_e = \dfrac{100}{P_e} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5 \text{ cm}$

For the eye to be least strained, the final image must be formed at infinity. This requires the intermediate image formed by the objective to lie exactly at the first focal point of the eyepiece. Thus, the object distance for the eyepiece is:

$u_e = f_e = 5 \text{ cm}$

The tube length $L$ of the microscope is the distance between the objective and the eyepiece:

$L = v_o + u_e$

$25 = v_o + 5 \Rightarrow v_o = 20 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula for the objective to find the object distance $u_o$:

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$

$\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{4} = -\dfrac{4}{20} = -\dfrac{1}{5} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$u_o = -5 \text{ cm}$

The linear magnification produced by the objective is:

$m_o = \left| \dfrac{v_o}{u_o} \right| = \left| \dfrac{20}{-5} \right| = 4$

The angular magnification produced by the eyepiece (acting as a simple microscope focused at infinity) is:

$m_e = \dfrac{D}{f_e} = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5$

The total angular magnification of the optical instrument is:

$M = m_o \times m_e = 4 \times 5 = 20$

Answer: $20$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An astronomical telescope is to be designed with a magnifying power of $50$ in normal adjustment. If the length of the tube is $102 \text{ cm}$, determine the powers of the objective and the eyepiece.
questions.solution:
For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the magnifying power is $m = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$ and the tube length is $L = f_o + f_e$.

Given $m = 50$, we have $\dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = 50 \Rightarrow f_o = 50 f_e$.

Given $L = 102 \text{ cm}$, substituting $f_o$ gives $50 f_e + f_e = 102 \text{ cm}$.

$51 f_e = 102 \text{ cm} \Rightarrow f_e = 2 \text{ cm} = 0.02 \text{ m}$.

The focal length of the objective is $f_o = 50 \times 2 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ cm} = 1 \text{ m}$.

The power of the objective is $P_o = \dfrac{1}{f_o} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1 \text{ D}$.

The power of the eyepiece is $P_e = \dfrac{1}{f_e} = \dfrac{1}{0.02} = 50 \text{ D}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An astronomical telescope's eyepiece has a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$. When the telescope is focussed for normal vision of distant objects, the tube length is $1.0 \text{ m}$. Determine the focal length of the objective and the magnifying power of the telescope.
questions.solution:
For normal vision, the final image is formed at infinity. The tube length of the telescope is given by $L = f_o + f_e$.

Given $L = 1.0 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}$ and $f_e = 10 \text{ cm}$.

$100 = f_o + 10$

$f_o = 90 \text{ cm}$

The magnifying power of the telescope for normal vision is given by $M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$.

$M = \dfrac{90}{10} = 9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Galilean telescope measures $27 \text{ cm}$ in length when it is focussed to produce an image at infinity. Determine the focal length of the eyepiece, given that the objective has a focal length of $30 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
For a Galilean telescope in normal adjustment (image at infinity), the length of the telescope tube is given by the difference between the focal length of the objective and the magnitude of the focal length of the eyepiece.

$L = f_o - f_e$

Given that the length of the telescope $L = 27 \text{ cm}$ and the focal length of the objective $f_o = 30 \text{ cm}$.

Substituting the given values:

$27 = 30 - f_e$

$f_e = 30 - 27 = 3 \text{ cm}$

The focal length of the eyepiece is $3 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A farsighted person is unable to see objects placed closer than $50 \text{ cm}$. Determine the power of the lens required to see objects located at $20 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
For a farsighted person, the lens must form a virtual image of the object at the person's near point.

Given object distance, $u = -20 \text{ cm}$

Image distance, $v = -50 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-50} - \dfrac{1}{-20}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = -\dfrac{1}{50} + \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{-2 + 5}{100} = \dfrac{3}{100} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

The focal length of the lens is $f = \dfrac{100}{3} \text{ cm} = \dfrac{1}{3} \text{ m}$

The power of the lens is given by $P = \dfrac{1}{f(\text{in m})}$

$P = +3 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nearsighted person cannot clearly see past $200 \text{ cm}$. Determine the power of the lens required for the person to view objects at large distances.
questions.solution:
For a nearsighted (myopic) eye, the lens must form an image of an object at infinity at the far point of the eye.

Given the far point is $200 \text{ cm}$, the image distance is $v = -200 \text{ cm} = -2 \text{ m}$.

The object distance is $u = -\infty$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-2} - \dfrac{1}{-\infty}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = -0.5 \text{ m}^{-1}$

The power of the lens is $P = \dfrac{1}{f} = -0.5 \text{ D}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person wears glasses with a power of $-2.5 \text{ D}$. Is the person farsighted or nearsighted, and what is the far point of the person without the glasses?
questions.solution:
The power of the lens is given as $P = -2.5 \text{ D}$.

Since the power is negative, the lens is concave. A concave lens is used to correct nearsightedness (myopia).

The focal length of the lens is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-2.5} \text{ m} = -0.4 \text{ m} = -40 \text{ cm}$.

For a nearsighted eye, the corrective lens forms a virtual image of an object at infinity at the person's far point.

Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$ with $u = -\infty$, we get $v = f = -40 \text{ cm}$.

The far point of the person without glasses is $40 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A professor reads a greeting card received on his $50$th birthday using $+2.5 \text{ D}$ glasses, holding the card $25 \text{ cm}$ away. Ten years later, he reads his farewell letter using the same glasses, but he must hold the letter $50 \text{ cm}$ away. Determine the power of the lens he should now use.
questions.solution:
Using the lens formula in terms of power, $P = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$.

At age $60$, the professor uses the same glasses with power $P = +2.5 \text{ D}$ to read the letter at a distance $u = -50 \text{ cm} = -0.5 \text{ m}$. The image is formed at his new near point $v$.

Substituting the values to find the vergence of his near point:

$\dfrac{1}{v} = P + \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = 2.5 + \left(\dfrac{1}{-0.5}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = 2.5 - 2.0 = 0.5 \text{ D}$

To read at the normal near point distance of $25 \text{ cm}$ ($u' = -25 \text{ cm} = -0.25 \text{ m}$), the new lens must form an image at this same near point $v$.

Let the new power required be $P'$. Using the lens formula again:

$P' = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u'}$

$P' = 0.5 - \left(\dfrac{1}{-0.25}\right)$

$P' = 0.5 - (-4.0) = +4.5 \text{ D}$

Therefore, the power of the lens he should now use is $+4.5 \text{ D}$.

Answer: $+4.5 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A normal eye has its retina positioned $2 \text{ cm}$ behind the eye-lens. Determine the power of the eye-lens when the eye is fully relaxed.
questions.solution:
When the eye is fully relaxed, it focuses parallel rays from an object at infinity onto the retina.

Object distance, $u = -\infty$

Image distance, $v = 2 \text{ cm} = 0.02 \text{ m}$

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{0.02} - \dfrac{1}{-\infty}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 50 \text{ m}^{-1}$

The power of the eye-lens is given by:

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = 50 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A normal eye has its retina positioned $2 \text{ cm}$ behind the eye-lens. Determine the power of the eye-lens when the eye is most strained.
questions.solution:
The image distance for the eye-lens is the distance to the retina, so $v = 2 \text{ cm} = +0.02 \text{ m}$.

When the eye is most strained, it focuses on an object placed at the near point. For a normal eye, the near point is at $25 \text{ cm}$.

The object distance is $u = -25 \text{ cm} = -0.25 \text{ m}$.

Using the lens formula, the power $P$ of the eye-lens is given by:

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$P = \dfrac{1}{0.02} - \dfrac{1}{-0.25}$

$P = 50 + 4 = 54 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The near point and the far point of a child are at $10 \text{ cm}$ and $100 \text{ cm}$, respectively. If the retina is located $2.0 \text{ cm}$ behind the eye-lens, determine the range of the power of the eye-lens.
questions.solution:
Using the lens formula, the power of the eye-lens is given by $P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$, where $v$ and $u$ are in meters.

The image distance is fixed at the retina, so $v = +2.0 \text{ cm} = +0.02 \text{ m}$.

For the far point, the object distance is $u = -100 \text{ cm} = -1.0 \text{ m}$.

The minimum power of the eye-lens is:

$P_{\text{min}} = \dfrac{1}{0.02} - \dfrac{1}{-1.0} = 50 + 1 = +51 \text{ D}$

For the near point, the object distance is $u = -10 \text{ cm} = -0.1 \text{ m}$.

The maximum power of the eye-lens is:

$P_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{1}{0.02} - \dfrac{1}{-0.1} = 50 + 10 = +60 \text{ D}$

The range of the power of the eye-lens is $+51 \text{ D}$ to $+60 \text{ D}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nearsighted person is unable to see objects beyond $25 \text{ cm}$. Assuming the separation of the glass from the eye is $1 \text{ cm}$, determine the power of the lens required to view distant objects.
questions.solution:
For viewing distant objects, the object distance is $u = -\infty$.

The far point of the nearsighted eye is at $25 \text{ cm}$ from the eye.

Since the lens is placed $1 \text{ cm}$ from the eye, the image must be formed at the far point. Thus, the image distance from the lens is $v = -(25 - 1) \text{ cm} = -24 \text{ cm} = -0.24 \text{ m}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-0.24} - \dfrac{1}{-\infty}$

$f = -0.24 \text{ m}$

The power of the lens is given by:

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-0.24} = -4.166 \text{ D} \approx -4.2 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person has a near point at $100 \text{ cm}$. What power of lens is required to read at $20 \text{ cm}$ if they use a contact lens?
questions.solution:
The person wants to read at a distance of $20 \text{ cm}$. Therefore, the object distance is $u = -20 \text{ cm} = -0.2 \text{ m}$.

The near point of the person is $100 \text{ cm}$. The lens must form the image of the object at this near point. Therefore, the image distance is $v = -100 \text{ cm} = -1 \text{ m}$.

Using the lens formula, the power $P$ of the lens is given by:

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

Substituting the values of $v$ and $u$:

$P = \dfrac{1}{-1} - \dfrac{1}{-0.2}$

$P = -1 + 5 = +4 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person has a near point at $100 \text{ cm}$. What power of lens is required to read at $20 \text{ cm}$ if they use spectacles having glasses $2.0 \text{ cm}$ separated from the eyes?
questions.solution:
The object is to be placed at a distance of $20 \text{ cm}$ from the eye.

Since the spectacles are $2.0 \text{ cm}$ away from the eyes, the object distance from the lens is:
$u = -(20 - 2.0) = -18 \text{ cm}$

The image must be formed at the near point of the person, which is $100 \text{ cm}$ from the eye. The image distance from the lens is:
$v = -(100 - 2.0) = -98 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-98} - \dfrac{1}{-18}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{18} - \dfrac{1}{98}$

The power of the lens $P$ is given by $P = \dfrac{100}{f}$ (where $f$ is in cm):
$P = \dfrac{100}{18} - \dfrac{100}{98}$

$P = 5.55 - 1.02 = +4.53 \text{ D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Priya wears $+1.5 \text{ D}$ glasses to achieve normal vision from $25 \text{ cm}$ onwards. She employs a $20 \text{ D}$ lens as a simple microscope to view an object. Determine the maximum magnifying power if she uses the microscope together with her glasses.
questions.solution:
The power of the simple microscope lens is given as $P = 20 \text{ D}$.

The focal length of the microscope lens is:
$f = \dfrac{100}{P} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5 \text{ cm}$

Priya wears glasses to achieve normal vision from $25 \text{ cm}$ onwards. When she uses the microscope together with her glasses, her eye effectively behaves as a normal eye with a near point (least distance of distinct vision) of $D = 25 \text{ cm}$.

The maximum magnifying power of a simple microscope is achieved when the final image is formed at the near point. The formula for maximum magnifying power is:
$M = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$

Substituting the values of $D$ and $f$:
$M = 1 + \dfrac{25}{5}$

$M = 1 + 5 = 6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Priya wears $+1.5 \text{ D}$ glasses to achieve normal vision from $25 \text{ cm}$ onwards. She employs a $20 \text{ D}$ lens as a simple microscope to view an object. Determine the maximum magnifying power if she uses the microscope without her glasses.
questions.solution:
Let the near point of Priya's eye without glasses be $D'$.

Using the lens formula for her glasses to achieve normal vision from $25 \text{ cm}$ ($u = -0.25 \text{ m}$):

$P = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$1.5 = \dfrac{1}{-D'} - \dfrac{1}{-0.25}$

$1.5 = -\dfrac{1}{D'} + 4$

$\dfrac{1}{D'} = 4 - 1.5 = 2.5 \text{ m}^{-1}$

$D' = \dfrac{1}{2.5} \text{ m} = 0.4 \text{ m} = 40 \text{ cm}$

The focal length of the simple microscope lens is:

$f = \dfrac{1}{P_{m}} = \dfrac{1}{20} \text{ m} = 5 \text{ cm}$

The maximum magnifying power of a simple microscope is obtained when the final image is formed at the near point of the observer. Since Priya uses the microscope without her glasses, her near point is $D' = 40 \text{ cm}$.

The maximum magnifying power $m$ is given by:

$m = 1 + \dfrac{D'}{f}$

$m = 1 + \dfrac{40}{5}$

$m = 1 + 8 = 9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A woman cannot see objects closer than $40 \text{ cm}$ from her left eye and closer than $100 \text{ cm}$ from her right eye. During a hiking expedition, she is separated from her group. She attempts to build an astronomical telescope from her reading glasses to look for her companions. Which lens should she use as the eyepiece?
options: Either lens, as they yield identical magnification
Neither lens, because reading glasses use concave lenses
questions.solution:
The woman is suffering from hypermetropia, so she uses convex lenses for reading.

For the left eye, the near point is $40 \text{ cm}$. Using the lens formula with $v = -40 \text{ cm}$ and $u = -25 \text{ cm}$:

$\dfrac{1}{f_{L}} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-40} - \dfrac{1}{-25} = \dfrac{3}{200} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$f_{L} = \dfrac{200}{3} \text{ cm}$

For the right eye, the near point is $100 \text{ cm}$. Using the lens formula with $v = -100 \text{ cm}$ and $u = -25 \text{ cm}$:

$\dfrac{1}{f_{R}} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-100} - \dfrac{1}{-25} = \dfrac{3}{100} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$f_{R} = \dfrac{100}{3} \text{ cm}$

Since $f_{L} > f_{R}$, the left lens has a larger focal length than the right lens.

In an astronomical telescope, the magnifying power is given by $M = \dfrac{f_{o}}{f_{e}}$. To achieve high magnification, the objective lens should have a larger focal length and the eyepiece should have a smaller focal length.

Therefore, the right lens, which has the smaller focal length, should be used as the eyepiece.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A woman cannot see objects closer than $40 \text{ cm}$ from her left eye and closer than $100 \text{ cm}$ from her right eye. During a hiking expedition, she is separated from her group. She attempts to build an astronomical telescope from her reading glasses to look for her companions. What magnification can she achieve with a relaxed eye?
questions.solution:
For reading glasses, the object distance is taken as the standard near point, $u = -25 \text{ cm}$. The lenses form virtual images at the respective near points of the defective eyes.

For the left eye, the image distance is $v_L = -40 \text{ cm}$. Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f_L} = \dfrac{1}{v_L} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f_L} = \dfrac{1}{-40} - \dfrac{1}{-25} = \dfrac{-5 + 8}{200} = \dfrac{3}{200} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$f_L = \dfrac{200}{3} \text{ cm}$

For the right eye, the image distance is $v_R = -100 \text{ cm}$. Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f_R} = \dfrac{1}{v_R} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f_R} = \dfrac{1}{-100} - \dfrac{1}{-25} = \dfrac{-1 + 4}{100} = \dfrac{3}{100} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$f_R = \dfrac{100}{3} \text{ cm}$

An astronomical telescope requires an objective lens with a larger focal length and an eyepiece with a smaller focal length to achieve a magnification greater than $1$.

Thus, the objective focal length is $f_o = f_L = \dfrac{200}{3} \text{ cm}$ and the eyepiece focal length is $f_e = f_R = \dfrac{100}{3} \text{ cm}$.

The magnification of an astronomical telescope for a relaxed eye (normal adjustment) is given by:

$M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$

$M = \dfrac{\dfrac{200}{3}}{\dfrac{100}{3}} = 2$
